extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users (especially authors of mathematical documents) preparing manuscripts with the AMS-LaTeX (amstex/amsart/amsbook) package; users migrating from AMS-TeX/TeX to LaTeX
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for installing and using the AMS-LaTeX package (amstex option and the amsart/amsbook documentstyles) to typeset mathematics with AMS conventions, including font selection, math commands, environments, and compatibility notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation requirement: new LaTeX format file for full installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation instructions for the ams-latex package require making a new LaTeX format file; however, this User’s Guide can be typeset without creating the new format file so users can read it before installing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to amltinst.tex for installation details. You can read the User’s Guide without the new format, but some sample-output demonstrating amstex-option commands may not be shown unless the new format is installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: For best understanding, you should be reasonably familiar with the LaTeX manual (Leslie Lamport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading The Joy of TeX (manual for plain-TeX) helps but is not mandatory; users with a plain-TeX background should consult the appendix describing differences between AMS-TeX and the amstex option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentstyle declarations for using amstex/amsart/amsbook
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the amstex option with a standard article: \documentstyle[amstex]{article}; alternatively use \documentstyle{amsart} or \documentstyle{amsbook} (these automatically include the amstex option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsart/amsbook as AMS-flavored equivalents of article/book when preparing manuscripts for AMS; amsart/amsbook auto-load amstex so no separate amstex option is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major package components
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS-LaTeX package consists of (1) the amstex option (a modification of AMS-TeX adapted to LaTeX) and (2) the amsart and amsbook documentstyles designed for AMS manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amstex if you want AMS-TeX-like math facilities within standard LaTeX; use amsart/amsbook when preparing AMS-style articles/books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font selection scheme attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mittelbach–Schöpf font selection scheme classifies fonts by four attributes: shape, series, size, and family; each attribute can be changed independently via \shape, \series, \size, and \family, and the new attributes take effect on \selectfont.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change multiple attributes and then call \selectfont. Example: \family{cmtt}\shape{n}\selectfont switches to Computer Modern typewriter family with current size/series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape attribute values and commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape values: normal (n), italic (it), small caps (sc), slanted (sl), upright italic (u). Commands: \shape{sc}\selectfont and abbreviations \sc, \it, \sl, \normalshape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note \normalshape replaces old \rm as a shape-changing command; with grouping most documents avoid frequent explicit \normalshape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series attribute (weight and width) and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Series is a combination of weight and width (e.g., light/medium/bold and condensed/expanded); use \series{...}\selectfont to choose a series. Abbreviations include \bf (\series{bx}) and \mediumseries (\series{m}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine weight and width abbreviations dropping m's except when both medium; examples: ubc (ultra bold condensed), sbc (semibold condensed), m (medium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Size attribute: \size takes two arguments (size and baselineskip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \size{<size>}{<baselineskip>}\selectfont to change font size and baselineskip together; baselineskip must include units (e.g., 18pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All common LaTeX size commands are defined in terms of \size. Provide units for baselineskip because units other than pt may be desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family attribute and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: A font family groups fonts sharing design features; select families via \family{<name>} or change document defaults with \renewcommand\rmdefault{...}, \sfdefault, \ttdefault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After changing defaults, \rm, \sf, and \tt select the new default families. To access Computer Modern explicitly use \family{cmtt}\selectfont.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defaults for attribute defaults (\bfdefault, \itdefault, \scdefault, \sldefault)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are defaults controlling which series/shape are used for \bf, \it, etc.; normal values: \bfdefault=bx, \itdefault=it, \scdefault=sc, \sldefault=sl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can change these defaults with \renewcommand to affect whole-document behavior (e.g., \renewcommand{\sldefault}{it} to make slanted fonts come out italic).

rubrics_metrics.name: oldlfont option to emulate pre–font-selection-scheme behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding the option oldlfont to documentstyle options emulates the old font selection scheme: size changes reset shape/series to normal/medium, \rm/\tt/\sf give normal shapes and medium series of respective families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use oldlfont if you need legacy behavior when migrating older documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font substitution warnings and overfull hbox font-name format
rubrics_metrics.description: When a font attribute combination is unavailable a nearest-font substitution occurs and a warning message indicates which font was substituted. Overfull hbox messages show fonts as family/series/shape/size (e.g., \cmr/bx/n/10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect warnings rather than errors for missing combinations; consult the warning message to know which font was used as substitute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math font commands differ from text font commands
rubrics_metrics.description: In AMS-TeX math font commands are not simple switches but commands that typically take one argument (e.g., \bold{A}) rather than scoped text switches like {\bf A}; amstex provides math font commands \mathrm, \bold, \cal, and (with AMSFonts) \frak, \Bbb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \newmathalphabet in the preamble to add new math alphabets. For bold nonalphabetic math symbols use \boldsymbol; for single-letter bold math use \bold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining and using additional math alphabets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \newmathalphabet*{\cmd}{<family>}{<series>}{<shape>} in the preamble to create a command for a new math alphabet; optionally add bold versions with \addtoversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \newmathalphabet*{\cy}{UWCyr}{m}{n} then use \cy{A}; to make bold available add \addtoversion{bold}{\cy}{UWCyr}{b}{n} so \boldsymbol{\cy{A}} or \boldmath produce bold versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold math symbols and fallbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: \boldsymbol is to be used for bold Greek and nonalphabetic math symbols; \pmb ('poor man’s bold') can be used when bold fonts are not available, but may not work well for large operators/extension symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define short macros for frequently used bold symbols (e.g., \newcommand{\bpi}{\boldsymbol{\pi}}). Be aware \pmb may not preserve spacing/limits for large operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: \newsymbol and amsfonts usage
rubrics_metrics.description: \newsymbol creates control sequences for symbols from AMS extra symbol fonts (MSAM, MSBM); when using AMSFonts without amstex, include 'amsfonts' in documentstyle options instead of \loadmsam / \loadmsbm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place \newsymbol commands in the preamble like \newcommand. The amsfonts option expects AMSFonts v2.0; earlier versions may require upgrade.

rubrics_metrics.name: amssymb option for convenience (requires extra memory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amssymb documentstyle option defines all ~200 AMS extra symbol names for convenience, avoiding many individual \newsymbol commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amssymb may require extra control sequence memory; consider including it in a custom format file to save processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary math spacing commands and fine tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary math spacing commands include \, (\thinspace), \: (\medspace), \; (\thickspace) and negative counterparts \! (\negthinspace), @, @! giving one-tenth spaces for fine tuning; these commands are robust and usable outside math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these for fine manual spacing adjustments; remember @, @! are finer fractions (one-tenth) of \, and \! etc. Use sparingly and prefer semantic spacing where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple integral commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \iint, \iiint, \iiiint for double/triple/quadruple integrals with properly adjusted spacing; \idotsint produces integrals with dots between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available in both text and display styles; use \idotsint when integrals should show dots between signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over and under arrow commands and scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides additional over/under arrow commands: \underleftarrow, \underrightarrow, \overleftrightarrow, \underleftrightarrow; these are modified to scale properly in subscript sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and output can be seen in sample file testart.tex after installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic dots commands (\dots and specialists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \dots and let placement be selected by following token; when context is ambiguous (end of formula) use semantic forms: \dotsc (commas), \dotsb (binary ops/relations), \dotsm (multiplication), \dotsi (integrals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This semantic approach increases portability across conventions. \ldots and \cdots remain available for compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math accents: properly positioned double accents and helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalized accent commands like \Hat, \Breve, \Vec, \Check, etc., position double accents properly (e.g., \Hat{\Hat A}); \accentedsymbol can predefine commonly double-accented symbols to speed processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \accentedsymbol{\Ahathat}{\Hat{\Hat A}} in the preamble to store results for quick retrieval. Use \sphat, \spddot, \spcheck, etc., for putting accents into superscripts more easily. \dddot and \ddddot provide triple/quadruple dot accents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots: use \leftroot and \uproot to adjust root indices
rubrics_metrics.description: When root index placement is unsatisfactory use \leftroot and \uproot to shift the index horizontally and vertically: e.g., \sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{2}\beta]{k}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments are in small units suitable for fine adjustments; negative leftroot moves index to the right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxed formulas: \boxed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \boxed{...} to put a box around math-mode content (similar to \fbox but for math).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for highlighting single displayed equations or parts of formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensible arrows for diagrams (@>>> and @<<<)
rubrics_metrics.description: @>>> and @<<< produce arrows that extend automatically to accommodate wide subscripts/superscripts; superscript text is typed between the first and second > (or <), subscript between second and third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally for commutative diagrams; requires loading the amscd option for extensible arrows to function properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \overset, \underset, and \sideset usage
rubrics_metrics.description: \overset{A}{B} places A above B (superscript-size), \underset places below; \sideset allows placing extra symbols at the subscript and superscript corners of large operators (e.g., to add primes and limits simultaneously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \sideset{<left>}{<right>}\sum_{...} to add corner symbols; note \stackrel is a more limited equivalent for superscripting relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: \text command for words/phrases in displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \text{...} in displays for text phrases; it is similar to \mbox but easier for subscripts (avoids explicit \scriptsize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer \text for readability and semantic clarity over \mbox in math subscripts/superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining operator names: \operatorname{...}
rubrics_metrics.description: \operatorname{xxx} produces operator names (e.g., log, sin) in roman with correct spacing in math, avoiding confusion with math italic variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because \operatorname is verbose, define shortcuts for frequently used operators if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraction and continued-fraction commands (and changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraction-related commands include \frac, \dfrac, \tfrac, \cfrac, and variants; \thickfrac and \thickfracwithdelims from AMS-TeX are replaced by square-bracket options on \frac and \fracwithdelims in amstex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section 21 for precise syntax and for continued fractions use the provided commands (e.g., \cfrac) for nicer output.

rubrics_metrics.name: New LaTeX environments: cases, matrix, Sb, Sp, commutative diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides new environments: 'cases' environment, matrix-related constructs, Sb and Sp, and commutative diagrams via the amscd option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unusual matrix column formatting use array; smallmatrix environment exists as a reimplemented \smallmatrix. Load amscd when using commutative diagrams or extensible arrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment/display environments and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex converts multi-line display commands to LaTeX-style environments: align, gather, alignat, multline, split, and provides alignment structures that may be used as entire displays or inside other displays; provides \intertext for interline text and controls for equation numbering and vertical spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \displaybreak before the \\ where it should take effect; use \notag or \nonumber where appropriate; see Section 25 for details on page breaks and error messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting fragile commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Fragile commands may need protection when used in moving arguments (e.g., section headings); amstex discusses protecting fragile commands as in standard LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \protect where necessary or define robust equivalents in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences from AMS-TeX and superseded commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Many AMS-TeX commands are superseded or reimplemented: e.g., document structure commands mapped to LaTeX equivalents, \roman renamed \mathrm, math style shorthand commands (\dsize, \tsize, etc.) dropped, \comment replaced by verbatim comment environment, and several global AMS-TeX commands made into LaTeX documentstyle options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Appendix B for detailed mappings and changes; when porting AMS-TeX documents, expect to refactor or replace commands with LaTeX equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsart and amsbook documentstyle specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: amsart and amsbook provide AMS-styled top matter, memory-conservation measures, running heads, non-English automatic text, theorem/proof handling, and other specialized behaviors for AMS manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amsart/amsbook automatically include amstex; consult Part IV for details on top matter, theorems, proofs, and differences from standard LaTeX article/book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BibTeX for bibliographies (bibliography styles provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography commands from the Joy of TeX were dropped in favor of BibTeX; amsplain and other .bst files are provided for use with BibTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer BibTeX-based workflows for bibliographies when using amsart/amsbook/amstex.

rubrics_metrics.name: New documentstyle options and modular features
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides options such as amssymb, amsfonts, amscd, amsbsy, amstext, and others for modular inclusion of features; some features are only available when options are loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load only the options you need (to save memory). Some options (e.g., amscd for diagrams) are required for specific features to function (extensible arrows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory usage and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining amstex with LaTeX produces a large macro package that can strain implementations of TeX (control sequence name limits, main memory); large bibliographies, many custom commands, and many cross-references increase the risk of overruns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor memory usage; avoid excessive personal definitions, large bibliographies, or preload fewer fonts; consider using format files or implementations with larger memory; see Table 6 (memory statistics) for example usage numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preloading fonts increases font memory usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Using different preload files (preload.min vs more preloaded fonts) will increase font memory usage and may push the implementation toward limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minimal preloads where possible; amsart tends to use fewer large fonts in headings so its font count can be smaller.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get help and report problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Send comments/questions to AMS Technical Support and include (1) the source file (with irrelevant material removed) and (2) a LaTeX transcript (log) file showing the error message and version numbers of style/option files used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact info: American Mathematical Society Technical Support (address, phone, Internet) is provided; include the minimal reproducible source and the log when reporting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global option mappings from AMS-TeX to LaTeX options
rubrics_metrics.description: Several global AMS-TeX commands that changed documentwide behavior (e.g., \TagsOnRight, \CenteredTagsOnSplits, \LimitsOnInts, \NoLimitsOnNames, \NoLimitsOnSums) are implemented as LaTeX documentstyle options in amstex; the opposite commands were dropped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corresponding documentstyle options to set these global behaviors; \TagsAsMath was dropped as marginally useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility notes for certain standard LaTeX commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Some standard LaTeX commands may not reset all font attributes under the new font-selection scheme (e.g., \footnote inside italic text remains italic because \footnote resets only size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need a normal-shape footnote inside italic text write \footnote{\normalshape ...}. Anticipate similar cases and add explicit font commands where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutative diagrams provided as separate option (amscd)
rubrics_metrics.description: To conserve memory, commutative diagram commands are provided in the amscd option and must be explicitly loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amscd must be listed in the documentstyle options to use CD environment and features like extensible arrows; some legacy commands (e.g., \pretend...\haswidth) are not available—use \hspace in subscripts/superscripts as an alternative.
